question: does x^2-N deviate from size-matched randomness in B-smoothness at u=log(v)/log(B) in {5,6,7,8}?

config.bin_def: bin w = v in [B^w, B^(w+1)), u = ln(v)/ln(B)
config.u_note: u binned by ACTUAL candidate magnitude (the numbers whose smoothness is tested); 'x_max-ish' read as the size of v itself
config.u78_truncation: with N<=2^80 and j<=3s the reachable v tops out near 15*s^2 ~= 3.75*N, so bin 7 tops out around u~7.9 and bin 8 around u~8.5; achieved ranges reported empirically per bin
config.control_match: exact (bitlen, mantissa-octant) histogram match; controls uniform within octant, candidates near-uniform in v
config.tester: gcd-chain primorial, shared code path both populations

assert_pipeline.reference: exhaustive strip of all primes<=1000, zero early exits

calibration.rho_prior_note: priors used ONLY for time allocation, not results

quotas.allocation: fixed time fractions (robust to unknown rates)

trend.model: OLS of log r*(u) on u; bootstrap over N-clusters

verdicts.verdict_detail: all u>=6 CIs cover 1; tightest 95% upper bound on |r-1| is 0.2168 at bin u=6

paper130_context: paper 130: ratios 0.88-0.91 at scales 2^32-2^44 (u<4.75), attributed to finite-x Dickman correction shared with controls; this experiment asks whether ANY O(1) relative deviation emerges at u>=5, where sieving's L_N[1/3] exponent lives
